data.narrative:
General Galactic, a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Halen Mattison and Luke Neise, has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers in Climate & Energy, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, alongside one public comparable (LNZA).

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $10M as a proxy baseline, a typical Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $25M. This method captures the expected progression in valuation discipline as the company advances from Seed funding. A Peer-Median approach is not applicable; while nine same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, none satisfied narrow filtering criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), and an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M (low) to $29M (high), with a median of $25M. This single-method triangulation carries material uncertainty. The range reflects standard Seed-stage progression assumptions but is constrained by the absence of tightly comparable peers at this stage and valuation tier. Key uncertainties include the company's specific technology differentiation within the fragmented Climate & Energy sector and near-term funding trajectory, both of which would warrant re-assessment as the company approaches Series A.
